oil.summary: Crude sold off hard on Tuesday, with WTI dropping 2.03% to $68.09/bbl and Brent off 2.44% to $71.14/bbl, extending a brutal month that has erased more than 25% from both benchmarks. The dominant macro driver is the US decision to temporarily ease Russian oil sanctions — reportedly to tame a price surge — which rattled European allies and injected fresh supply-side relief into the market. That move overshadowed what would normally be bullish data: the EIA reported a 3.8-million-barrel draw in US crude inventories for the week ending June 26. On the geopolitical side, Ukrainian drone strikes on two major Russian refineries forced Moscow to begin importing refined gasoline from India by sea, with Putin publicly acknowledging a 'difficult period' for domestic fuel supply. Markets appear to be pricing the sanctions easing as the dominant signal, with options markets assigning a 77% probability of an OPEC production decrease at the next meeting.
drivers: US temporarily eases Russian oil sanctions, overriding bullish inventory and geopolitical risk signals and pressuring prices lower
EIA reports a 3.8-million-barrel US crude inventory draw for w/e June 26, providing partial support that was insufficient to offset macro bearish flow
Ukrainian drone strikes ignite major Russian refineries; Russia begins importing gasoline from India, with Putin admitting domestic fuel shortages

gas.summary: Henry Hub slipped 1.95% on the day to $3.211/MMBtu, though the monthly picture remains modestly positive at +1.01%. TTF edged down 0.68% to €43.15/MWh but is up 5.56% on the week, suggesting European gas markets remain better supported than US benchmarks. News flow for the sector is thinner than oil today. JERA, Japan's largest LNG buyer, announced the creation of a standalone trading subsidiary to manage LNG, upstream, and low-carbon fuel businesses — a structural development that signals continued institutional investment in the global LNG supply chain. Saudi Aramco and Algeria cut July LPG contract prices amid swelling global supply, applying modest bearish pressure to gas-adjacent markets. Middle East producers have continued LNG loadings despite reported ship attacks in the region.
drivers: Henry Hub falls nearly 2% on the day; TTF holds weekly gains of over 5%, reflecting divergent US vs. European gas market dynamics
JERA creates a standalone LNG and low-carbon fuels trading arm, underscoring long-term institutional commitment to global LNG markets
Saudi Aramco and Algeria slash July LPG contract prices as global supply increases, adding bearish pressure to gas-adjacent commodities

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs dipped 0.67% to $75.36/EUA and are off 1.43% on the week, though the monthly trend remains marginally positive at +0.54%. The headline structural story is Germany recording a record 58% renewable share of electricity consumption in H1 2026, up from 55.8% in the same period last year — a milestone that carries long-run bearish implications for carbon demand in the power sector. European industry is split over the upcoming ETS overhaul, with companies voicing divergent concerns about the scheme's revamp. On the investment side, KKR agreed to acquire EDF Power Solutions North America for $4.2 billion, described as the largest single renewable energy investment the firm has ever made. Europe's nuclear ambitions are also drawing attention, with a uranium exploration firm in northern Italy reportedly planning a London listing to capitalise on renewed interest in nuclear power.
drivers: Germany hits a record 58% renewable share of electricity consumption in H1 2026, structurally bearish for long-run carbon demand in the power sector
KKR acquires EDF Power Solutions North America for $4.2 billion in its largest-ever clean energy deal, signalling strong private capital appetite for renewables
EU ETS overhaul debate intensifies as European industry voices split concerns, adding regulatory uncertainty to the carbon market outlook
